payload.title: cycle-snapshot-latest.json promotion has been dead 18 days — nominal-vs-actual HH:MM mismatch

root_cause.summary: Step 4.7 names the snapshot file from the ACTUAL fire minute; Step 6.0 looks it up by the NOMINAL tick minute. They agree only at drift_min==0.
root_cause.failure_line: emitPressureStateTool.ts:232-233 — existsSync(cycle-snapshot-12:00.json) is false => return {promoted:false, stale:false}

evidence: emit_pressure_state returned cycle_snapshot_promoted=false this tick (tick_id=2026-07-25T12:00:00Z, file on disk=cycle-snapshot-12:10.json).
cycle-snapshot-latest.json mtime 2026-07-07T21:47:54Z — 18 days stale while pressure-state.json updates every tick.
Zero of the 7 cycle-snapshot-HH:MM.json files on disk sit on a :00/:15/:30/:45 boundary (00:10, 08:10, 09:08, 12:10, 20:09, 20:26, 21:09).
drift_min observed 7, 7, 12 across this session — the dispatcher never fires at drift 0, so the lookup never hits.
stale:false in the return distinguishes this from the FIX-CYCLE-SNAPSHOT-STALE-PROMOTE-FAILSAFE freshness gate — this is a plain file-not-found, not a refusal.
blast_radius: cycle-snapshot-latest.json is frozen at 2026-07-07 for every consumer that reads it.
telemetry.md Step 6.0 sources last_regime and last_volatility_level from that file; both are therefore permanently unknown.

computeTiers maps volatility_level unknown -> volatility_tier low, so the high-volatility rows of cadence-policy.json are unreachable — the adaptive cadence volatility dimension is dead code in production.
This is the concrete mechanism behind the known 2-of-3-adaptive-inputs-dead observation; prior fix attempt UC-CDC-P1 did not close it.
secondary_findings: cadence-policy.json has NO row for calendar_status=closed, but pressure-state.json emits closed live. Table covers only open/half_day/holiday/weekend/unknown. Every off-hours lookup silently falls to the evaluateCadence 240-min safe default rather than a declared policy.
policy_id=alert-commander-critical has ZERO rows in cadence-policy.json for any calendar_status — a slot named critical always gets the generic 240-min default.
Both degrade safely (no crash, no suppression) which is why neither has ever surfaced.
payload.suggested_fix_direction: Make writer and reader share one key. Either pass the actual FILE_TICK back into emit_pressure_state instead of deriving from tick_id, or have Step 4.7 name the file by the nominal tick boundary. Prefer the latter — the nominal tick is already the stable per-tick identity used by the election lock. Add a regression test that fires the dispatcher at non-zero drift and asserts cycle_snapshot_promoted=true.
payload.action_taken: None — cowork-team is a dispatcher and does not mint board rows or edit apps/. Reported for PO triage.
payload.note: Tick itself completed normally: 3 slots matched, won, spawned, last_fired written, all locks released.
